headline.caveat: All-cash — Google's largest acquisition ever. Signed Mar 18, 2025; closed in 2026 after an extended DOJ antitrust review.

nature_md: Alphabet acquired cloud-security company Wiz for $32B in cash — its largest deal ever, roughly 2.5x the failed 2024 approach at ~$23B that Wiz walked away from to pursue an IPO. Wiz (CNAPP; ~$500M+ ARR at signing, targeting $1B) joins Google Cloud but is committed to remaining multicloud across AWS/Azure — securing rival clouds is part of the strategic value. Signed with a reported ~$3.2B reverse termination fee given antitrust risk; closed in 2026 after DOJ review.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Alphabet paid from its cash pile; Wiz consolidates into Google Cloud revenue from close, with the bulk of the $32B landing as goodwill/intangibles (revenue multiple ~50-60x at signing). Immaterial to Alphabet's balance sheet, headline-setting for security M&A comps.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Wiz's VC holders (Index, Sequoia, Insight, Cyberstarts) realized one of the largest venture cash exits ever; founders and employees cashed out at close rather than via IPO.

both_sides_md: **Bull:** Google Cloud buys the fastest-growing security franchise in history and neutralizes a gap versus Microsoft's security bundle — paid in cash it cannot otherwise deploy. **Bear:** ~60x ARR for a multicloud-committed asset inside a hyperscaler is a cycle-top comp; the 18-month regulatory limbo also froze Wiz's momentum against rivals.

sources.notes: Close timing per 2026 reporting; exact close date to be firmed up.
